:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors



$$
\mathbf{a_1}=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}, \quad \mathbf{a_2}=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{bmatrix}, \quad \mathbf{a_3}=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 2 \\ 3\end{bmatrix}, \quad \mathbf{b}=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 1 \\ 7\end{bmatrix}.
$$



If $x_1 \mathbf{a}_1 + x_2\mathbf{a}_2 + x_3\mathbf{a}_3 = \mathbf b,$ then what is $x_1+x_2+x_3?$
:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
Since $\mathbf{b}$ is a linear combination of vectors $\mathbf{a_1}, \,\mathbf{a_2}$ and $\mathbf{a_3}$ with coefficients $x_1,\, x_2$ and $x_3,$ respectively, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3} & =b \\ {x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{3}\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 2 \\ 3\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 1 \\ 7\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}0 \\ {x}_{1} \\ 0\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}{x}_{2} \\ 0 \\ -{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}{x}_{3} \\ 2{x}_{3} \\ 3{x}_{3}\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 1 \\ 7\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}{x}_{2}+{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{1}+2{x}_{3} \\ -{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3}\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 1 \\ 7\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{2}+{x}_{3} &=1 \\ {x}_{1}+2{x}_{3} &=1 \\ -{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3} &=7\end{aligned}\right.
$$

We will solve this system using Gaussian elimination. First, we write the augmented matrix for this system:



$$
M= \left[ \begin{array}{ccc|c}0 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 & 3 & 7\end{array} \right]
$$



Row-reducing the augmented matrix, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\begin{bmatrix}0 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 & 3 & 7\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 & 3 & 7\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 4 & 8\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3} & :=\frac{1}{4}{R}_{3} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 2\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{3} &=1 \\ {x}_{2}+{x}_{3} &=1 \\ {x}_{3} &=2.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

From the third equation, we get $x_3 = 2.$ Substituting this into the second equation, we get

$$
x_2+(2) = 1 \quad\Rightarrow\quad x_2 = -1,
$$

and substituting $x_3=2$ into the first equation, we get

$$
x_1+2(2) = 1 \quad\Rightarrow\quad x_1 = -3.
$$

So the solution of the system is $x_1=-3, x_2=-1, x_3=2,$ which means

$$
-3 \mathbf{a_1}- \mathbf{a_2} +2 \mathbf{a_3}= \mathbf{b}.
$$

Consequently,

$$
x_1+x_2+x_3=-3-1+2=-2.
$$

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{a}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{bmatrix},\,{a}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{bmatrix},\,{a}_{3}=\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 0 \\ 5\end{bmatrix},\,b=\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{bmatrix}.
$$

If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3}=b,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}?$
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3}=b$, then we have  

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{3}\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 0 \\ 5\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1} \\ 0 \\ {x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}-{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}2{x}_{3} \\ 0 \\ 5{x}_{3}\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}+2{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+5{x}_{3}\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}+2{x}_{3} &=2 \\ {x}_{2} &=3 \\ {x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+5{x}_{3} &=-1\end{aligned}\right.
$$

We will solve this system using Gaussian elimination. First, we write the augmented matrix for this system:

$$
M=\begin{bmatrix}1 & -1 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 3 \\ 1 & 1 & 5 & -1\end{bmatrix}
$$

Row-reducing the augmented matrix, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\begin{bmatrix}1 & -1 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 3 \\ 1 & 1 & 5 & -1\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & -1 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 2 & 3 & -3\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-2{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & -1 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & -9\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{3} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & -1 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -3\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}+2{x}_{3} &=2 \\ {x}_{2} &=3 \\ {x}_{3} &=-3.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

From the third equation, we get ${x}_{3}=-3$ and from the second equation we get ${x}_{2}=3.$ Substituting these into the first equation, we obtain

$$
{x}_{1}-3+2(-3)=2\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=11.
$$

So, the solution of the system is ${x}_{1}=11$, ${x}_{2}=3$, and ${x}_{3}=-3,$ which means 

$$
11{a}_{1}+3{a}_{2}-3{a}_{3}=b.
$$

Consequently, 

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=11+3-3=11.
$$

$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3} &=-2 \\ 2{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2}+2{x}_{3} &=-6 \\ 3{x}_{1}+6{x}_{2}+9{x}_{3} &=7\end{aligned}\right.
$$

We will solve this system using Gaussian elimination. First, we write the augmented matrix for this system:

$$
M=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & 3 & -2 \\ 2 & 5 & 2 & -6 \\ 3 & 6 & 9 & 7\end{bmatrix}.
$$

Row-reducing the augmented matrix, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & 3 & -2 \\ 2 & 5 & 2 & -6 \\ 3 & 6 & 9 & 7\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & 3 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & -4 & -2 \\ 3 & 6 & 9 & 7\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & 3 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & -4 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 13\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}

$$

Consider the vectors

$$

$$

If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3}=b,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}?$
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3}=b$, then we have  

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 3 \\ -2\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}-3 \\ -8 \\ 6\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{3}\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 5 \\ -3\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1} \\ 3{x}_{1} \\ -2{x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}-3{x}_{2} \\ -8{x}_{2} \\ 6{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}2{x}_{3} \\ 5{x}_{3} \\ -3{x}_{3}\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2}+2{x}_{3} \\ 3{x}_{1}-8{x}_{2}+5{x}_{3} \\ -2{x}_{1}+6{x}_{2}-3{x}_{3}\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2}+2{x}_{3} &=2 \\ 3{x}_{1}-8{x}_{2}+5{x}_{3} &=1 \\ -2{x}_{1}+6{x}_{2}-3{x}_{3} &=2\end{aligned}\right.
$$

We will solve this system using Gaussian elimination. First, we write the augmented matrix for this system:

$$
M=\begin{bmatrix}1 & -3 & 2 & 2 \\ 3 & -8 & 5 & 1 \\ -2 & 6 & -3 & 2\end{bmatrix}
$$

Row-reducing the augmented matrix, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\begin{bmatrix}1 & -3 & 2 & 2 \\ 3 & -8 & 5 & 1 \\ -2 & 6 & -3 & 2\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & -3 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -5 \\ -2 & 6 & -3 & 2\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & -3 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 6\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2}+2{x}_{3} &=2 \\ {x}_{2}-{x}_{3} &=-5 \\ {x}_{3} &=6.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

From the third equation, we get ${x}_{3}=6.$ Substituting ${x}_{3}=6$ into the second equation, we obtain

$$
{x}_{2}-6=-5\,⟹\,{x}_{2}=1.
$$

Now, substituting ${x}_{2}=1$ and ${x}_{3}=6$ into the first equation, we obtain

$$
{x}_{1}-3(1)+2(6)=2\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=-7.
$$

So, the solution of the system is ${x}_{1}=-7$, ${x}_{2}=1$, and ${x}_{3}=6,$ which means 

$$
-7{a}_{1}+{a}_{2}+6{a}_{3}=b.
$$

Consequently, 

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=-7+1+6=0.
$$

$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-5{x}_{2}-{x}_{3} &=1 \\ 2{x}_{1}-8{x}_{2}+2{x}_{3} &=9 \\ -{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2}+{x}_{3} &=1\end{aligned}\right.
$$

$$

Row-reducing the augmented matrix, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\begin{bmatrix}1 & -5 & -1 & 1 \\ 2 & -8 & 2 & 9 \\ -1 & 5 & 1 & 1\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & -5 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 & 4 & 7 \\ -1 & 5 & 1 & 1\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & -5 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 & 4 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 2\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-5{x}_{2}-{x}_{3} &=1 \\ 2{x}_{2}+4{x}_{3} &=7 \\ 0 &=2.\end{aligned}\right.

However, the final equation $0=2$  gives a false statement. So the system has no solution.

Consider the vectors

$$

$$

If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3}=b,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}?$
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3}=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 0 \\ 4\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}-2 \\ -5 \\ -1\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{3}\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ 11 \\ -2\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ -4 \\ 15\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1} \\ 0 \\ 4{x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}-2{x}_{2} \\ -5{x}_{2} \\ -{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}3{x}_{3} \\ 11{x}_{3} \\ -2{x}_{3}\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ -4 \\ 15\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3} \\ -5{x}_{2}+11{x}_{3} \\ 4{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}-2{x}_{3}\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ -4 \\ 15\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3} &=2 \\ -5{x}_{2}+11{x}_{3} &=-4 \\ 4{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}-2{x}_{3} &=15\end{aligned}\right.
$$

We will solve this system using Gaussian elimination. First, we write the augmented matrix for this system:

$$
M=\begin{bmatrix}1 & -2 & 3 & 2 \\ 0 & -5 & 11 & -4 \\ 4 & -1 & -2 & 15\end{bmatrix}
$$

Row-reducing the augmented matrix, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\begin{bmatrix}1 & -2 & 3 & 2 \\ 0 & -5 & 11 & -4 \\ 4 & -1 & -2 & 15\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & -2 & 3 & 2 \\ 0 & -5 & 11 & -4 \\ 0 & 7 & -14 & -7\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & -2 & 3 & 2 \\ 0 & 7 & -14 & -7 \\ 0 & -5 & 11 & -4\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{7}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & -2 & 3 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & -5 & 11 & -4\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+5{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & -2 & 3 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the system is now 

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3} &=2 \\ {x}_{2}-2{x}_{3} &=1 \\ {x}_{3} &=1.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

From the third equation, we get ${x}_{3}=1.$ Substituting this value into the second equation, we get

$$
{x}_{2}-2(1)=1\,⟹\,{x}_{2}=3.
$$

Finally, by substituting ${x}_{2}=3$ and ${x}_{3}=1$  into the first equation, we obtain

$$
{x}_{1}-2(3)+3(1)=2\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=5.
$$

So, the solution of the system is ${x}_{1}=5$, ${x}_{2}=3$, and ${x}_{3}=1,$ which means 

$$
5{a}_{1}+3{a}_{2}+{a}_{3}=b.
$$

Consequently, 

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=5+3+1=9.
$$
